clearedSpotChecks.check: Which keccak routine the official X Layer image runs for KECCAK256, pool ids (src/types/PoolId.sol:14) and position keys (src/libraries/Position.sol:60). Result claimed: the image enables no Cargo feature and nothing in the manifests turns on alloy-primitives/asm-keccak, so KECCAK256 runs through the sha3 crate and keccak-asm is not compiled.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The conclusion that keccak-asm is not compiled is wrong, so the correction of cycle 32 should be withdrawn. The research read bin/node/Cargo.toml, DockerfileOp and justfile correctly: FEATURES and RUSTFLAGS default to empty (DockerfileOp:46-50, :76) and bin/node has default = [] (bin/node/Cargo.toml:75). It missed that bin/node depends on reth.workspace = true (bin/node/Cargo.toml:28), and the workspace entry reth = { git = "https://github.com/okx/reth", rev = "f60420a..." } (Cargo.toml:88) does not set default-features = false. The package named reth at okx/reth f60420a is bin/reth, whose default feature list includes asm-keccak (bin/reth/Cargo.toml:85-94), and asm-keccak there enables alloy-primitives/asm-keccak (bin/reth/Cargo.toml:113-117). Cargo unifies that feature across the build, so the official image compiles alloy-primitives with keccak-asm. With RUSTFLAGS empty it is the generic x86_64 routine and not the AVX-512 one, which matches what cycle 32 said. The practical result of the item still holds on the endpoint as served: my own 1,800 vector rerun and the unit's 120 KECCAK256 pairs and every pool id and mapping slot in the script sets match. What is wrong is the stated reason, and with it the claim that L-1202 concerns only operator-built nodes.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Owner, protocol fee controller and code of the PoolManager on both chains. Result claimed: code 24,009 bytes with the recorded sha256 prefixes, owner 0x044aaf33...b6b7, protocolFeeController the zero address, so no fee can be set.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran it at latest. eth_call 0x8da5cb5b (owner(), selector checked with tools/opdiff/evm.py keccak) returned 0x044aaf330d7fd6ae683eec5c1c1d1fff5196b6b7 on https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech. eth_call 0xf02de3b2 (protocolFeeController()) returned the zero word on both. eth_getCode gave 24,009 bytes with sha256 prefixes 86106cb2c6688f82 (Celo) and 395c56a54ab2e08c (X Layer). src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and :48 revert unless msg.sender equals protocolFeeController, and no public transaction on either chain can have the zero address as sender. Celo's fee currency debit and credit calls run with caller zero, but their target is the registered fee currency and never the PoolManager, so they do not reach these lines. Only the owner can change the controller (src/ProtocolFees.sol:29). That makes it governance only.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Rerun of battery.py (99,985 vectors) and targeted.py (85,544 vectors) on forno.celo.org and rpc.xlayer.tech, all returning the specified word.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The logs in the unit's work directory (out/battery.log, out/targeted.log, out/pinned-forno.json) show 0 mismatches and 0 errors. I built a separate loop dispatcher with my own vectors (cycles/034/op-stack-custom-gas.work/verify/spot.py). It ran 1,800 vectors on each chain: 200 each of MULMOD and ADDMOD, including modulus 2^256-1 as used at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, and of SDIV, SMOD, SAR, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, SHR and SHL, with TickMath limits and limb boundaries as edge values. All 1,800 matched the specification on both chains (verify/spot.json). Forno's two backends were not pinned in my run. The unit's pinned run covers that.
